solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: In the morning, gripped compass (5)

blocks.note: am = ante meridiem, before noon
bit = gripped with the teeth

annotation.surface: A hiker grabs their compass first thing in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compass' is the magnetic instrument in the surface, but here it means range or scope, the sense of 'within the compass of'.
annotation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or extent of something, which is what a compass means in 'beyond my compass'.

entries.clue: Nearly missing over border (4)

indicators.note: the word is lacking the next item, so it is taken out

blocks.note: about = nearly, as in 'about ten'
O = over, the cricket abbreviation; it is removed

annotation.surface: A near miss on the frontier line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border' is a verb here: to abut is to border on something.
annotation.definitionFit: Things that abut each other border each other, sharing an edge.

entries.clue: I’m surprised to be embraced by British Nobel laureate (4)

indicators.note: the exclamation is held inside the abbreviation, as if hugged

blocks.note: Br = British, the standard abbreviation
oh! = an exclamation of surprise, placed inside BR

annotation.surface: Someone is astonished to be hugged by a British prize winner.
annotation.walkthrough: Niels Bohr was Danish, so 'British' is not part of the definition; it supplies BR and the laureate stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr won the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on atomic structure.

entries.clue: Italian stronghold in Otranto periodically offers retaliation (3,3,3)

indicators.note: the first part goes inside the letters from Otranto
take letters at regular intervals: the 2nd, 4th and 6th

blocks.note: the even letters of oTrAnTo, which wrap around the rest
It = Italian, the abbreviation
a fort is a stronghold; IT + FORT sits inside T…AT

annotation.surface: An Italian castle town strikes back at its attackers.
annotation.walkthrough: Otranto is a real fortified town in southern Italy, which makes the surface convincing; it is only raw material for TAT.
annotation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is paying back a wrong with a like one, which is retaliation.

entries.clue: Hated communist encapsulates wickedness (7)

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it like a capsule

blocks.note: a red = a communist
vile = wicked; placed inside RE…D

annotation.surface: A loathed communist embodies evil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wickedness' is a noun but gives the adjective VILE; the clue asks for the idea, so solvers accept the loose part of speech.
annotation.definitionFit: Reviled means abused and despised, so strongly hated.

entries.clue: Hackneyed output on the subject of mess (6)

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in a memo heading
to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it

annotation.surface: Tired old writing about some muddle.
annotation.walkthrough: A rehash is old material served up again, hence hackneyed output.
annotation.definitionFit: A rehash is something produced by reworking old material, which is stale, hackneyed output.

entries.clue: Energy provider’s centre opening in May (3)

indicators.note: take the middle two letters of the word
take the first letter of the word

blocks.note: the middle two letters of proVIder
the first letter of May

annotation.surface: The heart of a power company opens in May.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Energy provider' reads as a utility company, but the definition is just 'Energy'.
annotation.definitionFit: Vim is vigour or liveliness, a word for energy.

entries.clue: Mourned for soldiers among deceased 500 (8)

indicators.note: one part is placed in the middle of another

blocks.note: the late = the deceased
men = soldiers, as in 'officers and men'; placed inside LA…TE
D = 500 in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A memorial to five hundred fallen soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a war memorial, so every word seems to belong to the definition; only 'Mourned for' does.
annotation.definitionFit: To lament someone is to mourn them, so lamented means mourned for.

entries.clue: Separate record on damaged tree (8)

indicators.note: the letters of the word are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: a disc = a record, as in vinyl
the letters of TREE rearranged

annotation.surface: A record lies apart, resting on a broken tree.
annotation.walkthrough: Don't confuse with DISCREET (tactful): DISCRETE means distinct or separate.
annotation.definitionFit: Discrete means individually distinct, existing as separate parts.

entries.clue: Release one French jerk (7)

blocks.note: un = one in French
a hitch is a sudden jerk or tug

annotation.surface: Setting free a French idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for the Frenchman, but it means a sudden pull, which is a hitch.
annotation.definitionFit: To unhitch a horse or trailer is to release it from what holds it.

entries.clue: Notes, a few minutes, sent over (5)

indicators.note: turned over, so written back to front

blocks.note: some = a few
m = minutes, the abbreviation

annotation.surface: A few quick notes are dispatched after a couple of minutes.
annotation.walkthrough: The commas make 'a few minutes' look like a time delay, but it splits into SOME and M.
annotation.definitionFit: Memos are short written notes passed around an office.

entries.clue: Perhaps bone is a mess (4,6)

blocks.note: a bone is an example of what a dog eats
a muddle or botched job; this sense is British slang

annotation.surface: A bone left lying around is untidy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a bone as just one example of a dog's dinner. In British slang, making a dog's dinner of something means making a mess of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A dog's dinner is British slang for a mess, and literally a bone could be one.

entries.clue: Preface reduction, somehow (9)

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An editor cuts a book's preface down somehow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preface' is a verb here: to preface a talk is to introduce it.
annotation.definitionFit: To preface something is to introduce it with opening remarks.

entries.clue: Criminal studied entrance to prison in question (8)

indicators.note: wrong or bad, so the letters go astray
the first letter, the way into the word

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the first letter of prison, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A crook who studied is questioned on arriving in jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the person being questioned, but it only tells you to mix up the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A matter in question is being disputed, argued over and not settled.

entries.clue: Make repairs along said passage (8)

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is what you hear rather than how it is spelt

blocks.note: over = along, as in 'walk over the bridge'
a hall is a passage; HAUL sounds the same in British speech

annotation.surface: A builder fixing things along a narrated corridor.
annotation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the R, HALL and HAUL sound alike.
annotation.definitionFit: To overhaul an engine is to take it apart and repair it thoroughly.

entries.clue: Welcome in first of trainees in brief inspection (6)

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the shortened word
take only the first letter
cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: the word in, used as itself
a view is an inspection; brief loses the W
the first letter of trainees, placed inside VI…E

annotation.surface: A new trainee is welcomed in with a short look around.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's with different jobs: the first is taken literally, the second is a container instruction. A view is an inspection, and 'brief' trims its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: asking someone to come along is making them welcome.

entries.clue: Static rates should change with time (2,4)

indicators.note: the letters are to be altered into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
t = time, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Frozen interest rates ought to move eventually.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is economics: static rates that need to change over time. 'Static' is the definition, meaning not moving.
annotation.definitionFit: Something at rest is not moving, which is what static means.

entries.clue: Lecherous type lowers large coat (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving a letter lower means moving it further along the word

blocks.note: a luster is one who lusts
L = large, moved down one place from LUSTER

annotation.surface: A lecher drops his big overcoat.
annotation.walkthrough: An ulster is a long, loose overcoat with a cape, named after the Irish province. The letters of LUSTER stay the same; only the L moves.
annotation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long heavy overcoat, originally made in Ulster.

entries.clue: Welsh town’s drunk part blotto (4,6)

indicators.note: the letters stagger about, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A Welsh town is partly drunk already.
annotation.walkthrough: Port Talbot is a steel town in South Wales. 'Blotto' means very drunk, so 'drunk' and 'blotto' seem to repeat each other; one is the indicator, one is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Port Talbot is an industrial town on the south Wales coast.

entries.clue: Joke cigars ultimately wrapped in black (4)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of cigars is used
the letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: jet = black, as in jet-black
the last letter of cigars, placed inside JE…T

annotation.surface: A prank involving cigars rolled in black paper.
annotation.walkthrough: Jet is a black mineral, hence jet-black.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a light-hearted remark made to amuse.

entries.clue: Starts to take up bronze age instrument (4)

indicators.note: take the starting letter of each following word

blocks.note: the first letters of Take Up Bronze Age

annotation.surface: An archaeologist unearths a Bronze Age musical instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bronze Age sounds like the date of the instrument, but those words are only there for their initials.
annotation.definitionFit: The tuba is a large brass wind instrument.

entries.clue: Fly back, retaining western accent (5)

indicators.note: a fly flying back travels the other way, so its letters are read right to left
the insect holds the letter inside it

blocks.note: a gnat is a small fly
W = western, placed inside GNA…T before the turnaround

annotation.surface: A fly returns, keeping a cowboy accent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Western' with 'accent' suggests a cowboy drawl, which a twang is, but in the wordplay it is just W.
annotation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal accent, like a Texan or Australian twang.

entries.clue: Backing essentially saved Hugo Boss (3)

indicators.note: the letters are turned around
at their essence, the middle letters

blocks.note: the middle letter of saVed
the middle letters of hUGo; 'essentially' covers both words

annotation.surface: Supporting the fashion label Hugo Boss saved it.
annotation.walkthrough: Hugo Boss is a fashion brand, so 'Boss' seems glued to 'Hugo'. Guv is British slang for boss, short for governor.
annotation.definitionFit: Guv, short for governor, is British slang for a boss.

entries.clue: Greek character grabs vulgar Canadian Liberal (7)

indicators.note: the outer word takes hold of the other word inside it

blocks.note: tau = the Greek letter T
rude = vulgar; placed inside T…AU

annotation.surface: A Greek man seizes a crude Canadian politician.
annotation.walkthrough: Pierre and Justin Trudeau were both Liberal prime ministers of Canada. 'Character' means a letter, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Justin Trudeau, like his father Pierre, led Canada's Liberal Party as prime minister.

entries.clue: Present first half of demo standing by organ (7)

indicators.note: keep only the first half of the word

blocks.note: the first two of the four letters of demo
the liver is an organ of the body

annotation.surface: A church organist plays the opening of a demo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a musical instrument, but it is the body part. 'Present' is a verb: to deliver a speech is to present it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: you present a speech or a verdict by handing it over formally.

entries.clue: Additional member of cast doing little (5)

blocks.note: more than is usual or expected
a film or stage performer hired to stand in the background

annotation.surface: A bit-part actor with almost nothing to do.
annotation.walkthrough: An extra in a film stands in the background, so does very little.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the adjective means more than usual, and the film noun is a background performer with no lines.
